meta.note: Provenance day: watermarks, camera attestation and platform labelling all landed at once.

stories.title: Claude gets invisible watermarks on text and images
stories.blurb: Anthropic will embed machine-readable marks in generated text and sign files to the C2PA standard, to comply with European AI transparency rules. Support is being extended to older models as well.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Claude will apply invisible watermarks to AI text and images

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.headline: Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its AI models

stories.title: Spotify puts a badge on AI artists and cuts them from recommendations
stories.blurb: From mid-September, profiles representing AI-generated identities carry an "AI Persona" label, and their music is excluded from editorial, algorithmic and personalised recommendations by default. A platform deciding that synthetic authorship is a distribution question, not just a disclosure one.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Spotify says it won’t recommend music from AI Personas

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.headline: Spotify will label AI Persona profiles and exclude their music from recommendations

stories.title: Apple looks at proving a photo came from a camera
stories.blurb: Code in the iOS 27 beta points to an "Apple Reference Image" system that would verify a photograph was taken with an iPhone camera. Attestation at capture, the counterpart to watermarking at generation.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Apple could help you prove your iPhone photos aren’t deepfakes

stories.title: Gemini hits a billion users, and 150 million images a day
stories.blurb: Google says Gemini is its fastest-growing product ever, with 63 percent of users talking to it by voice. The image number is the one worth holding on to: 150 million generations every day.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: ChatGPT and Gemini both just passed 1 billion users

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.headline: Google’s Gemini app surges to 1 billion users

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: Gemini becomes Google’s fastest-growing product ever as it hits 1B users

stories.title: ArtStation and Sketchfab change hands
stories.blurb: The sale merges two of the places digital artists use to show and store work into one integrated ecosystem spanning the whole creative process. Creative Bloq asks what that consolidation means for the artists on both platforms.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: What does the sale of ArtStation and Sketchfab mean for digital artists?

stories.title: A studio denies it replaced its writers with ChatGPT
stories.blurb: A former lead writer says Saber "replaced me with ChatGPT"; the CEO says neither Saber nor Unigine replaced any writers with AI. The dispute is unresolved and it is the shape of a lot of credit fights to come.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Saber denies replacing Rideshare Stimulator’s writers with ChatGPT

stories.title: She lost a business to AI and bet the rest on the hand
stories.blurb: Nosheen Ahmed worked as a dentist for two decades before calling herself an illustrator. With AI flooding publishing, she is making the case for handmade work as the position, not the fallback.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: How Nosheen Ahmed lost her side business to AI, and bet her whole career on the human hand

stories.title: "We treat code as material"
stories.blurb: Studio Dial moves between a cocktail menu one day and motion design for entire city plans the next. The line about code as material is the useful part: a studio that treats the medium as something you shape rather than something you order from.

sources.name: It's Nice That
sources.headline: “We treat code as material”: Studio Dial weaves motion design into cocktail menus, Afghan textiles and city plans

stories.title: Architecture serving art direction, with Lottie
stories.blurb: Alexey Kopytin walks through the build of a tactile web experience and argues the technical architecture has to serve the art direction, not the other way round. Rare to see that dependency written down.

sources.name: Smashing Magazine
sources.headline: Building Tactile UX: Honoring Intentional Design With Lottie

stories.title: An archive of the letterforms nobody photographs
stories.blurb: Kwazi Design's years-long typographic project documents Kolkata's everyday lettering and the hyper-local context behind it. Attention as a method, applied to type that was never meant to be looked at twice.

sources.name: It's Nice That
sources.headline: Type Around Town asks us to pay attention to the letterforms that surround us every day

stories.title: 7UP redraws itself for the first time in 15 years
stories.blurb: The biggest change to the identity, and to the taste, since 2011. Creative Bloq expects it to be contentious, which is the normal fate of a mass-market refresh.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: The new 7UP rebrand is bound to be contentious

stories.title: Almost every commercial image is retouched, and nobody costs it in
stories.blurb: Tímea Buknicz on why post-production stays invisible in credit and in budget, despite sitting in the path of nearly every commercial image. A live question now that generative tools are entering the same step.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Design View with Retoucher of the Year founder Tímea Buknicz
